title: Global minimum cut: all bipartitions vs Stoer-Wagner
problem_statement: Given an undirected graph on n vertices as an n x n symmetric matrix W of non-negative integer edge weights with zero diagonal (W[u][v] = 0 means no edge), compute the global minimum cut weight: the minimum, over all partitions of the vertex set into two non-empty sides S and V - S, of the total weight of the edges with one end in S and one in V - S. The graph need not be connected (then the answer is 0). Convention: for n < 2 no such partition exists and the answer is None.

input.size_measure: n^2 matrix entries (n(n-1)/2 independent weights). Weights are small integers in the harness; costs count weight additions and comparisons as unit-cost operations (with b-bit weights each one costs O(b + log n) bit operations, since every cut weight is at most n^2 2^b / 4).

algorithms.name: brute force
algorithms.idea: Fix vertex 0 on one side and enumerate the other side S over all 2^(n-1) - 1 non-empty subsets of {1, ..., n-1}; sum the weights over S x (V - S) for each and keep the minimum.
algorithms.pseudocode:
best = None
for each non-empty S subset of {1..n-1}:
    w = sum of W[u][v] over u in S, v not in S
    if best is None or w < best: best = w
return best
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2 2^n): exactly n(n-1)2^(n-3) weight additions and 2^(n-1) - 2 weight comparisons (n >= 2). In terms of the input size N = n^2 entries this is 2^Theta(sqrt(N)), still super-polynomial.
algorithms.correctness: Exhaustive: every partition into two non-empty sides has exactly one side not containing vertex 0, and that side is one of the enumerated sets S.

algorithms.name: Stoer-Wagner (array)
algorithms.idea: n - 1 phases. Each phase orders the current vertices by maximum adjacency (repeatedly add the vertex most tightly connected to the set built so far); the last vertex t against the rest is a minimum s-t cut for the last two vertices s, t. Record it, merge t into s, repeat; the answer is the lightest recorded cut.
algorithms.pseudocode:
best = None; active = all vertices
while |active| > 1:
    a = first active vertex; key[v] = W[a][v] for the others
    repeat |active| - 1 times: sel = argmax key over unadded vertices; mark sel added; key[v] += W[sel][v] for the unadded v
    s, t = last two vertices added; best = min(best, key[t])
    merge t into s: W[s][v] += W[t][v] for every other active v; remove t
return best
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) with plain arrays: a phase on k vertices costs Theta(k^2); exactly (n-1)(n-2)(n+3)/6 weight additions and n(n-1)(n-2)/6 + n - 2 weight comparisons (n >= 2).
algorithms.correctness: Stoer & Wagner 1997, Theorem (cut-of-the-phase lemma): in a maximum-adjacency ordering ending in s, t, the cut ({t}, rest) is a minimum s-t cut. The global minimum cut either separates s and t (and weighs at least the cut of the phase) or does not (and survives merging s and t). Induction over the n - 1 phases. Same argument as Nagamochi & Ibaraki 1992 in simplified form.

relationship: Exponential -> polynomial on the same problem: the brute force performs Theta(n^2 2^n) weight operations (exactly n(n-1)2^(n-3) additions + 2^(n-1) - 2 comparisons), Stoer-Wagner Theta(n^3) (exactly (n-2)(2n^2+n+3)/6 additions + comparisons). The brute force ignores the structure of minimum cuts: the cut-of-the-phase lemma lets Stoer-Wagner merge two vertices after each phase instead of trying all partitions. Stoer & Wagner 1997 also give O(nm + n^2 log n) with a Fibonacci heap (m = number of edges); on dense matrix input (m = Theta(n^2)) that is Theta(n^3) as well, so the array version is the right one here. Karger-Stein's randomized recursive contraction (1996; O(n^2 log^3 n), recalled, not re-checked against the paper) is faster but not implemented.

verification.method: V1: both implementations agree with each other and with an independent harness.check on 96 instances (sizes 0-12, 16, 20, 24; 6 trials; brute force up to n = 12). generate mixes six families: dense weights 0..9, sparse (often disconnected), two components by construction, a planted light cut between two dense halves, a weakly attached vertex, and the all-zero matrix; on the validator's seeds the minimum cut is 0 in 47 of the 84 instances with n >= 2 and 79 contain zero off-diagonal entries. check computes min over t = 1..n-1 of the maximum 0-t flow (Edmonds-Karp written in the harness; max-flow = min-cut, and every global cut separates 0 from some t) and, for n <= 10, also enumerates all vertex subsets with a different formula (degree sum minus twice the inside weight); for n < 2 it requires None. Negative controls (experiments/2026-10-07b_global_min_cut_counts.py): check rejects answer+1 on 84/84 instances, the minimum weighted degree on 28/84, Stoer-Wagner's first phase alone on 34/84. V2 (exact counts, RL-047 method): the harness's CountingWeight counts every weight addition and order comparison made by the UNCHANGED implementations; reported_cost = additions + comparisons. Proven closed forms, checked for brute force n = 2..14 and Stoer-Wagner n = 2..40, 48..256: brute force n(n-1)2^(n-3) + 2^(n-1) - 2; Stoer-Wagner (n-1)(n-2)(n+3)/6 + n(n-1)(n-2)/6 + n - 2 = (n-2)(2n^2+n+3)/6; neither depends on the weights. Fits at tolerance 0.03: brute force on n = 6..14 (even) alpha = 1.002 against n^2 2^n, rivals n^3 2.838, 2^n 1.305, n 2^n 1.134, n^3 2^n 0.897 rejected; Stoer-Wagner on n = 32, 64, 128, 256 alpha = 1.007 against n^3, rivals n^2 2^n 0.037, n^4 0.755, n^2 1.510, n^2 log^3 n 1.128 rejected. |alpha - 1| comes only from lower-order terms; both fits also resolve the log-factor diagnostic (0.951/1.058 and 0.936/1.088). Timing is not used.

caveats: Costs count weight additions and comparisons as unit-cost operations (word-RAM); with b-bit weights each costs O(b + log n) bit operations. The input has N = n^2 matrix entries, so the brute force is 2^Theta(sqrt N) in the input size (super-polynomial, not 2^Theta(N)) and Stoer-Wagner is Theta(N^1.5). Loop overhead not involving weights (building the sides, list removals, index scans) is of the same order as the counted operations (Theta(n^2 2^n) and Theta(n^3)) but is not counted. Convention: for n < 2 the answer is None (no partition into two non-empty sides). The diagonal must be zero; both implementations ignore it, but the harness's subset oracle assumes it.
notes: Karger-Stein was considered as a third, classical-randomized algorithm (it would allow secondary tag T4 under the validator rule) and skipped: its V1 check would be probabilistic, the 45-minute budget favoured exact closed forms for the two deterministic algorithms, and the pattern report's timing analysis (rho = 1.050) shows timing could not separate n^3 from n^2 log^3 n. With exact counts the Stoer-Wagner implementation's counts do reject an n^2 log^3 n cost (alpha 1.128 at tolerance 0.03), so a counted Karger-Stein implementation would be a resolvable future addition.
